_notes: 1. These are verses from the Canticle of Moses (Deuteronomy 32), used as a canticle in the Office. The Vulgate verse numbers match the 思高 numbering directly for this passage. 2. 思高 v.2 splits 'like rain / like dew / like showers / like drops' across more lines than the Vulgate two-hemistich structure; the * mediant is placed to divide the two main images (rain/doctrine and dew/speech). 3. v.3: The Latin two hemistichs are 'like showers on grass, like drops on green' + 'for I will proclaim the name of the Lord'; the 思高 merges these; mediant placed at verse boundary. 4. v.11: 思高 reads 'according to the number of the angels' (天使的数目) for 'filios Israël' — following 思高's LXX-based reading; this is the 思高 text used verbatim. 5. v.16 (Latin 32:16 = Expándit alas…): the 思高 merges the eagle imagery across vv.11-12 differently; translation follows 思高 v.11b. 6. v.22 (Latin 32:22 = Incrassátus): 思高 v.15 uses the name 耶叔戎 (Jeshurun) which does not appear in the Vulgate wording but is in 思高; kept verbatim. 7. v.27 (Latin 32:27): 思高 says 'the rock that bore you' (磐石) where Latin says 'Deum qui te genuit'; 思高 wording used verbatim. 8. Basan (v.20) = 巴商 per 思高. 9. The canticle structural markers (*) are placed to reflect the Vulgate's two-hemistich division while using 思高 wording.
